verdict: Avoid new paper exposure in Kala Amb for now; the state signal is too weak to underwrite a commodity converter, so lend only to a proven, pulp-integrated or packaging-led borrower with tight structure.
title: Kala Amb Paper & Paper Products: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
Kala Amb is a Sirmour-district industrial town on the Haryana border whose units make paper, metal, chemicals and thread, with paper named among its core products [2]. A paper unit buys wood pulp or waste paper, cooks and bleaches it, runs it across paper machines, and sells reels or sheets to converters, printers and packaging buyers. Cash comes in only when the reel is dispatched and the buyer pays; cash goes out upfront for fibre, power and fuel. **So the whole credit question is whether the borrower's fibre and power cost sits below its realisable paper price, and how long its cash is tied up between those two points.**

## Where value and cash actually sit
Peers show the shape of the economics. Kuantum's digester work lifted pulp yield by 1% and cut steam use from 1.8 to 0.8 metric tons per ton of pulp [4] — energy and fibre conversion is where margin is made or lost. Pudumjee's March-quarter revenue rose to ₹201 crore from ₹190 crore with net profit at ₹20 crore [5], and Kuantum's Q4FY26 operating income grew 4% sequentially to ₹301 crore with EBITDA of ₹48 crore [6]. On working capital, a rated peer had to pay suppliers in advance while taking 45-60 days to recover from customers, forcing reliance on working-capital bank lines [8]. **So when a proposal lands, check the power and fibre cost per ton against the selling price per ton; if the borrower cannot show that spread, ask for the last six months of power bills and purchase invoices before you discuss limits.**

## What has changed now
Himachal's own demand signals are weak: GST collections are -22.8% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1%, and electricity demand is -6.8% against India's +9.5% [D]. Nationally, paper output (NIC 17) is -0.1% YoY even as overall output is +8.6% Apr-to-date [D]. Rating commentary flags volatile realisations hit by cheaper imports and exposure to input and energy costs [11], and wastewater-treatment failure can bring penalties and stop operations [10]. **So treat a Kala Amb paper proposal as a local-demand and commodity-price double exposure; if the borrower's sales are mostly within Himachal or to price-sensitive converters, ask what share of orders is repeat and priced monthly.**

## Where to grow, and how to grow safely
Pursue converters and packaging-led units with diversified buyers, and pulp-integrated players with own power; avoid standalone writing-and-printing mills selling into a falling realisation market. Structure limits against a borrowing-base of paid receivables, not stock alone, given the 45-60 day collection cycle peers report [8]. Take monthly stock-and-receivable statements, power bills and sales register; covenant a minimum EBITDA per ton and a cap on supplier advances. **If the borrower cannot give monthly power consumption and sales price per ton, do not sanction; ask for it as a condition precedent.**

## Early-warning signs
Watch for falling realisations against flat fibre cost, rising supplier advances, and any pollution-board notice. **If power consumption per ton rises or the buyer list shortens, cut the limit and move to receivables-only lending.**
